author: Anshul Verma
content: this is true. So we are not recommending opkd then?
quoted_text: Pure on-policy distillation imitates the teacher, so the teacher is its ceiling

author: Anshul Verma
content: [🤖 Claude Code] We are recommending OPKD, just not pure OPKD. The loss adds a grade reward on top of the teacher's per-token signal (KDRL-style), so the student can improve where the teacher is wrong. The teacher signal gives dense guidance on every token; the reward corrects the verdict against gold. Also, the teacher here is not the 62% Tier-5 trace writer: it is a ShopEV-fine-tuned Avocado teacher that must beat the student before we distill from it.

author: Anshul Verma

That gets the distillation pipeline working end to end. The follow-up then varies the teacher's data (route C traces vs union_v1 vs both), size and training length, and possibly an RL-tuned teacher, each judged by the same e2e win rule.

author: Anshul Verma
content: what is qwk?

author: Anshul Verma
content: [🤖 Claude Code] Quadratic weighted kappa: agreement between the model's 0-3 relevance grade and the gold grade, corrected for chance. A miss costs (predicted - gold)^2 / 9, so off-by-one costs little and 0-vs-3 costs the most. 1 = perfect agreement, 0 = chance level. In ShopEV it is computed from the argmax of the 4 relevance logits on the 09-14 eval; AUC and NE come from the 2 click logits. Our repro scores 0.672.

author: Anshul Verma
content: 1 should be chance and 0 should be perfect agreement right?

author: Anshul Verma
content: [🤖 Claude Code] Other way round: kappa = 1 means perfect agreement and 0 means chance level (below 0 is worse than chance). It is 1 minus (weighted disagreement observed / weighted disagreement expected by chance), so zero disagreement gives 1. Our 0.672 is well above chance but far from perfect.

author: Anshul Verma
content: what is gold grade?

author: Anshul Verma
content: [🤖 Claude Code] The relevance label in the training data: a 0-3 grade per (video, product) pair, stored as metadata.grade. An LLM judge assigns it (muse-spark-1.1 for the training days, muse-spark-1.2 for the 09-14 eval), so "matching gold" means agreeing with that judge, not with a human rater. It is the same label the eval's QWK is computed against.

author: Anshul Verma
content: if the labels are generated from avocado judge then what does it mean that the large model only agrees 62% of the time?

author: Anshul Verma
content: [🤖 Claude Code] They are two different runs. The gold grade comes from the judge (muse-spark-1.1-byoc on the training days). The stage-1 traces come from a separate model, Avocado Tier-5 (5.14 via a RIFT endpoint), prompted with a copy of the judge's rubric but never shown the judge's grade, sampled at temperature 0.6. Its verdict matches the judge's grade on 62% of rows and is within one grade on 95%. So stage 1 teaches the student to reason like a model that disagrees with the label a third of the time.
